projects.title: Logic and proof technique
projects.blurb: Propositions and truth tables, normal forms, proofs as Lean tactics, quantifiers, three kinds of induction, relations and well-founded termination: the toolkit every later course uses.

lessons.title: Propositions and truth tables
lessons.blurb: Why “if … then” is defined the way it is, truth tables, tautologies, and satisfying assignments as witnesses.

lessons.title: Equivalence and normal forms
lessons.blurb: A formula for any truth table, read off its rows; then the laws of logic as rewrites: negation normal form, CNF and DNF, one law a step.

lessons.title: Proofs as Lean tactics
lessons.blurb: Natural deduction in Lean: what it takes to prove each connective and what you can do with one, and proofs as programs.

lessons.title: Predicates and quantifiers
lessons.blurb: ∀ as a long ∧ and ∃ as a long ∨: counterexamples and witnesses, negation by De Morgan, the order of quantifiers, and quantifiers in Lean.

lessons.title: Induction on the natural numbers
lessons.blurb: Why checking is not enough, and induction as a recipe that produces a proof for any n: dominoes, sums, and proofs in Lean.

lessons.title: Strong induction
lessons.blurb: When the step needs more than the case before: prime factors, making change, and why strong induction, weak induction and well-ordering are one principle.

lessons.title: Structural induction
lessons.blurb: The same idea for anything defined by constructors: lists, trees, expressions, and a small simplifier proved sound.

lessons.title: Relations
lessons.blurb: When do two things count as the same? Properties with counterexamples, closures as what you are forced to add, equivalence classes, and a deduplication bug.

lessons.title: Well-founded relations and termination
lessons.blurb: No infinite descent: why a loop stops, cycles as counterexamples, measures as proofs, and termination in Lean.

projects.title: Order and lattices
projects.blurb: From Zero to Propagators: partial orders, lattices and fixed points; semilattices as merges, access decisions and information flow; Galois connections; and propagator networks in Lean, ending with a Sudoku solver.

lessons.title: Relations and partial orders
lessons.blurb: What "at most" has to mean: partial orders on numbers, divisibility and sets, Hasse diagrams, and the definitions in Lean.

lessons.title: Special elements and monotone maps
lessons.blurb: What replaces "the larger of two": bounds, joins and meets, when they fail to exist, and maps that respect the order.

lessons.title: Lattices
lessons.blurb: Posets where every pair has a join and a meet: duality, the standard examples, and distributivity.

lessons.title: Complete lattices and fixed points
lessons.blurb: Apply until nothing changes: complete lattices, the Knaster–Tarski theorem, and least fixed points by iteration.

lessons.title: Semilattices: the laws of a merge
lessons.blurb: Messages arrive in any order, grouped any way, twice: the three laws a merge needs, and the order every such merge hides.

lessons.title: A merge is a join
lessons.blurb: Records merged field by field and last-writer-wins registers: merges that are joins, built and proved in Lean.

lessons.title: Distributive and Boolean lattices
lessons.blurb: Does meet distribute over join? M₃ and N₅ as the witnesses, unique complements, and the Boolean lattices of sets and squarefree divisors.

lessons.title: Access decisions
lessons.blurb: Combining permit and deny: deny-overrides and permit-overrides are joins, first-applicable is not commutative.

lessons.title: Information flow
lessons.blurb: Denning's lattice of security classes: data may only flow up, and a computation's output gets the join of its inputs' classes.

lessons.title: Galois connections and closure operators
lessons.blurb: Best approximations between a fine order and a coarse one, the closure operators they make, and the concept lattice of a formal context.

lessons.title: Fixed points in practice
lessons.blurb: Apply until nothing changes: reachability as a least fixed point, why start at the bottom, and why the iteration stops.

lessons.title: The propagator model
lessons.blurb: Cells that only gain information, in a lattice; propagators as monotone functions between them; why the answer does not depend on the schedule.

lessons.title: A propagator network in Lean
lessons.blurb: Mutable cells that only grow, a scheduler that runs to quiescence, and a constraint that runs in every direction.

lessons.title: The interval lattice
lessons.blurb: Bounds on a number as partial information: intersection as the merge, interval arithmetic propagators, and what a contradiction does to termination.

lessons.title: Capstones: Sudoku and type inference
lessons.blurb: A Sudoku solver and a type checker, both as propagator networks over lattices of partial information.

projects.title: CRDTs: replicated data that converges
projects.blurb: From Propagators to Replicas: counters, sets and registers that replicas update without coordinating and merge as joins, each design the fix for the last one's bug; the main theorem that they converge; gossip, version vectors, op-based CRDTs, a replicated store, and the limits.

lessons.title: Replicas and the merge discipline
lessons.blurb: Two replicas lose an update; the three laws a merge needs so that the network cannot make it lose one: states in a semilattice, merge as join.

lessons.title: The G-Counter
lessons.blurb: Counting without coordination: why one number cannot be merged, and the fix, one slot per replica merged by pointwise maximum.

lessons.title: The PN-Counter
lessons.blurb: Counting down without going down: the decrement a merge undoes, and the fix, two grow-only counters and a value that subtracts.

lessons.title: Sets that only grow
lessons.blurb: G-Set and 2P-Set: union as the merge, the removal a merge brings back, tombstones, and the re-add they forbid.

lessons.title: Last writer wins
lessons.blurb: Overwrite, done lawfully: timestamps in the state, ties broken by replica, and what the merge silently throws away.

lessons.title: The OR-Set: add wins
lessons.blurb: Observed-remove: tag every add, and let a remove delete only the tags it has seen, so re-adds work and a concurrent add survives.

lessons.title: Multisets, folds and the main theorem
lessons.blurb: Why the three laws are exactly enough: drop one and a network breaks it; keep all three and the same updates give the same state, proved once for every CRDT.

lessons.title: Delivery: gossip, duplication and reordering
lessons.blurb: What the network may do to messages, why only loss matters, eventual delivery as the one requirement, and a gossip driver that provably stops.

lessons.title: Version vectors and causality
lessons.blurb: Time without clocks: record how much you have seen from each replica, which is the G-Counter again, and read concurrency as incomparability.

lessons.title: Op-based CRDTs
lessons.blurb: Shipping operations instead of states: what the join used to absorb becomes the network's job, commuting operations and exactly-once delivery.

lessons.title: Capstone: a replicated store
lessons.blurb: A collaborative shopping list from the course's parts: an OR-Set of items, each with a PN-Counter quantity, converging with no new proofs.

lessons.title: What CRDTs cannot do
lessons.blurb: Agreement is not correctness: a balance that converges below zero, invariants that need coordination, and the axiom audit.

projects.title: Transition systems, invariants and temporal logic
projects.blurb: A lost update as a path in a graph of states; invariants with counterexample traces and inductive proofs; a lock that fails and Peterson's that does not; safety and liveness under fairness; temporal logic as fixed points; happens-before, effectively-once delivery and refinement; rewriting systems, and retries under failure.

lessons.title: State machines and executions
lessons.blurb: Two threads that lose an update: a system as variables, an initial state and guarded actions, and its graph of reachable states as every interleaving at once.

lessons.title: Invariants and induction
lessons.blurb: What holds in every reachable state: refuted by a shortest trace, proved by one step of induction, and strengthened when that step fails.

lessons.title: Mutual exclusion
lessons.blurb: A lock built from a check and a take, the race the checker finds, two fixes (an atomic step, and Peterson's flags and turn), and an inductive proof.

lessons.title: Safety and liveness
lessons.blurb: Nothing bad happens; something good eventually does. Finite counterexamples and infinite ones, deadlocks and lassos, and the fairness a scheduler must promise.

lessons.title: Temporal logic as fixed points
lessons.blurb: Words for always and eventually, on some path and on every path; each one computed by repeating a step until nothing changes: least and greatest fixed points.

lessons.title: Happens-before
lessons.blurb: Without a shared clock, ask which event could have caused which: a partial order, a single counter that cannot capture it, and vector clocks that can.

lessons.title: Effectively-once delivery
lessons.blurb: A client that retries because it cannot tell a lost request from a lost reply; the duplicate that follows; and the idempotent handler that makes the effect happen once.

lessons.title: Refinement
lessons.blurb: An implementation's steps are the specification's steps or invisible ones: checking that one system implements another, and an operation-rewriting optimization proved sound.

lessons.title: Rewriting systems
lessons.blurb: Lesson 8's folds as rules on terms: rewriting to a normal form, termination by a measure, and confluence by critical pairs.

lessons.title: Retries and backoff
lessons.blurb: Retrying a call that fails at random: the chance that every attempt fails, the expected number of attempts, and the load and wait that backoff trades.

projects.title: Calculus: derivatives and integrals
projects.blurb: The slope at a point, found by zooming in; the power, product and chain rules read off pictures; the circle behind cos, sin and e^(it); tangent lines and bending; then antiderivatives the engine checks by differentiating, and area as slope run backwards.

lessons.title: The rules of differentiation
lessons.blurb: The slope at a point, as what secants settle on; the power rule from a growing square, the product rule from a growing rectangle.

lessons.title: The chain rule
lessons.blurb: Functions of functions: follow a nudge through the inner function and then the outer one, and see why the inner derivative comes out in front.

lessons.title: Circles, exponentials and rotation
lessons.blurb: Why e^(it) walks round the unit circle: cosine and sine as shadows, multiplying by i as a quarter turn, Euler's formula, angles that add, and arctan as an angle.

lessons.title: Tangent lines and the second derivative
lessons.blurb: The tangent line as the best straight stand-in for a curve, estimates from it, and the second derivative as how fast the curve bends away.

lessons.title: Antiderivatives, checked
lessons.blurb: Differentiation run backwards: guess a function with the given derivative, then check it by differentiating, as the engine does; substitution and parts as the chain and product rules undone.

lessons.title: Area and the fundamental theorem
lessons.blurb: The area under a curve from rectangles, then exactly: the area so far grows at the rate of the curve's height, so it is an antiderivative.

projects.title: Linear algebra: vectors, matrices and systems
projects.blurb: Vectors as arrows and as lists, matrices as moves of the plane, solving systems by elimination with verified row operations, and the determinant as the factor by which area scales.

lessons.title: Vectors: arrows, lists and the dot product
lessons.blurb: Adding arrows tip to tail, stretching them, reaching every point with two of them, length, and the dot product as a shadow.

lessons.title: Matrices as moves of the plane
lessons.blurb: A matrix records where the two unit arrows land; from that, where it sends any vector, and multiplying matrices as one move after another, in an order that matters.

lessons.title: Solving systems by elimination
lessons.blurb: Which input lands on a given output: elimination on the augmented matrix, row operations proved to keep the solutions, and the matrices that squash the plane, with no solution or infinitely many.

lessons.title: Determinants: how a matrix scales area
lessons.blurb: The determinant as the factor by which a matrix scales area, ad − bc from a picture, its sign as a flip, zero as squashing with no inverse, and why determinants multiply.

projects.title: λ-calculus I: computing with functions
projects.blurb: What if functions were the only thing? Terms, free and bound variables, substitution without capture, β-reduction and normal forms, evaluation strategies, de Bruijn indices, Church encodings and recursion by fixed points; an interpreter built in Lean alongside.

lessons.title: Terms and notation
lessons.blurb: A language with nothing but functions: variables, functions and applications, how they are written, and a first β-step.

lessons.title: Free and bound variables
lessons.blurb: Placeholders and outside values: which variables a λ binds, which are free, and why the names of bound ones do not matter.

lessons.title: Substitution and capture
lessons.blurb: The obvious substitution, two ways it goes wrong, and the renaming that fixes it.

lessons.title: β-reduction and normal forms
lessons.blurb: Chaining β-steps: where it stops, terms that never stop, why the order of steps cannot change the answer, and η.

lessons.title: Evaluation strategies
lessons.blurb: Which redex first: normal order, call by name, call by value, applicative order, and a term where the choice decides whether you finish.

lessons.title: De Bruijn indices
lessons.blurb: Terms without bound names: point at a variable's binder by counting λs, and α-equivalence becomes equality.

lessons.title: Church encodings
lessons.blurb: A thing is what you can do with it: booleans that choose, numerals that iterate, pairs, the predecessor puzzle, and lists.

lessons.title: Recursion and fixed points
lessons.blurb: How a function can call itself without a name: self-application, the Y combinator derived from ω, factorial, and Z for call by value.

projects.title: λ-calculus II: types and proofs
projects.blurb: The simply typed λ-calculus: typing rules and derivation trees, type inference by unification, what types rule out, propositions as types, type safety, polymorphism and dependent types, with the theory proved in Lean.

lessons.title: Simple types
lessons.blurb: What goes wrong without types, what a type has to record to prevent it, and the three typing rules that follow.

lessons.title: Typing derivations
lessons.blurb: Why Ω's half has no type, where a derivation gets stuck, shadowing, one type per term, and the checker proved sound.

lessons.title: Type inference
lessons.blurb: Types without annotations: unknown types as variables, the equations a term imposes, unification and the occurs check.

lessons.title: What types rule out
lessons.blurb: Ω and Y fail to type, every typed term stops, and what that costs.

lessons.title: Propositions as types
lessons.blurb: A type is a proposition, a term of it a proof: the Curry–Howard correspondence.

lessons.title: Type safety
lessons.blurb: Well-typed programs do not go wrong: progress and preservation, and a safety proof in Lean.

lessons.title: Polymorphism
lessons.blurb: One term at many types: type schemes, System F, and Church numerals that work at every type.

lessons.title: Dependent types
lessons.blurb: Types that depend on values; Lean's type theory; type checking is proof checking.

projects.title: Explorations
projects.blurb: Notebooks that show what ChalkMath does: a tour, Fourier series drawing a llama, and order theory with its proofs in Lean.

lessons.title: Welcome to ChalkMath
lessons.blurb: A short tour: running cells, reading the steps, and one example from each area.

lessons.title: Drawing llamas with circles
lessons.blurb: Fourier series from inner products to epicycles, ending with a llama drawn by spinning circles.

lessons.title: Order and lattices
lessons.blurb: Part I of From Zero to Propagators: partial orders, joins and meets, monotone maps and fixed points, with the proofs in Lean cells.
